description: Portable GraphQL processor scenarios for the closed load gates and confinement (§3.2), pinned-schema interpretation and live introspection (§3.3), and the staleness posture (§4). Peer shape for this family: `peer` is one scripted HTTP response `{status, contentType, body}`, or `{"sequence": [...]}` listing consecutive responses consumed in dispatch order; an entry `{"noResponse": true}` scripts a request that yields no response (connection, name-resolution, or TLS failure, or timeout). Observation paths: `/dispatch` is the last request the processor sent (`method`, `headers`, `body`, `url`), `/dispatches/<i>` the i-th request in order; `/outputs` the emitted operation values in order. Scenarios for §5 to §9 arrive with those sections.

scenarios.description: A location whose scheme is neither http nor https refuses at load, before any request.
A content object without a document member refuses at load.
A document that does not parse under the governing edition's grammar refuses at load.

content.document: query Viewer($id: ID!) { viewer(id: $id) { id name }

scenarios.description: A subscriptions member whose transport and location scheme do not pair refuses at load.
A schema that references an undefined type fails the schema-validity gate and refuses at load.

content.document: query Viewer($id: ID!) { viewer(id: $id) { id } }
content.schema: type Query { viewer(id: ID!): Person }

scenarios.description: A document whose every operation definition shares its name with another leaves no addressable target; the source refuses as a source at resolution.

content.document:
query A { status }
query A { status }

scenarios.description: A duplicated name destroys only the duplicated position's addressability; §5.2.2.1's failure is inventory-wide, so the sibling Status resolves and refuses before dispatch.
A structural introspection member (fields on User) absent at an element the selected operation reaches makes that operation invalid: it refuses before dispatch.
The same structural absence does not reach an operation that never touches the element: Status dispatches against the same pinned result.
An annotative member (isDeprecated on Query.viewer) absent at a reached element makes the operation lossy, not invalid: it dispatches with the carried document and variables unchanged.

A pinned October 2021 result lacks isOneOf on every element and is read as that edition's result: Filter is an ordinary input object, and an invocation carrying two of its members is dispatched, not refused (the OneOf limit of §3.3).
An introspection result whose queryType names a type absent from types references an undefined type: it fails the schema-validity gate and refuses at load.
With schema absent the processor sends exactly the capability probe by POST, then the introspection query composed from every capability the probe observed, then the operation.

assertions.equals: query { t: __type(name: "__Type") { fields { name args { name } } } f: __type(name: "__Field") { fields { name args { name } } } d: __type(name: "__Directive") { fields { name args { name } } } i: __type(name: "__InputValue") { fields { name } } }

scenarios.description: A June 2018 service: every probe position observes only the base members, so the composed query carries none of the later additions and no includeDeprecated argument on args or inputFields; the 2018-shaped result lacks isRepeatable and the __InputValue deprecation members, which the edition exceptions read as false and null.

A probe position that resolves to null selects the base selection for that type whatever the other positions observed: with t null, the composed query omits the __Type additions but keeps isRepeatable from d.
A request error result from the probe refuses the source at load, at gate 4; the composed query is never sent.
An execution result whose data is null from the composed query refuses the source at load, at gate 4.
Both introspection requests carry the configured protocolFields the invocation will carry, and remain POST when httpMethod selects get.
Both introspection requests carry the configured extensions map, so the schema observed is the one the invocation's request reaches.

A pinned schema is dispatched against as carried: the processor sends no introspection request, and a service that rejects the pin-validated document produces its own request error, which completes the invocation unsuccessfully with no output.

A service that has evolved beyond the pin returns a value the pinned contract does not admit; the invocation completes with that value as the operation's value (the second staleness face), and no re-introspection is attempted.

content.document: query Status { status }
content.schema:
type Query { status: Status }
enum Status { ACTIVE }

scenarios.description: Gate 5 applies to a live-introspected result as to a carried one: a live result whose queryType names a type absent from types refuses the source at load, and the operation is never sent.

A June 2018 introspection shape declares interfaces null on an INTERFACE element; that null is the sixth edition exception, read as the empty set, so an operation selecting through the interface is represented and dispatches.

content.document: query NodeQ($id: ID!) { node(id: $id) { id } }

scenarios.description: A composed-query result that carries an errors entry beside data.__schema fails gate 4 exactly as a carried object would, and the source refuses at load.
A probe request that yields no response reaches no gate: the load does not complete and the invocation refuses before dispatch for want of an interpreted schema, with no further request.
An operation reaches __Schema.directives through a directive used in a fragment it spreads: with directives absent from the pinned result, A is invalid and refuses before dispatch.
The sibling operation B uses no directive at any of its positions, so the absent directives member has no consequence for it and it dispatches.
With content.subscriptions absent, a subscription operation is accounted invalid for want of a target; its selector resolves and the invocation refuses before dispatch.

content.document:
query Status { status }
subscription Ticks { ticks }
content.schema:
type Query { status: String }
type Subscription { ticks: Int }

scenarios.description: The same source's query operation is unaffected by the absent subscriptions member and dispatches.

content.document:
query Status { status }
subscription Ticks { ticks }
content.schema:
type Query { status: String }
type Subscription { ticks: Int }

assertions.equals:
query Status { status }
subscription Ticks { ticks }

scenarios.description: Loading precedes every refusal below it: a schema-absent source is introspected (probe and composed query) even though the selected subscription, lacking a content.subscriptions target, then refuses before dispatch with no operation request.

content.document:
query Status { status }
subscription Ticks { ticks }

scenarios.description: A present selector resolves to the operation definition of that exact name and dispatches.
An absent selector over a lone anonymous operation resolves to it and dispatches.

content.document: { status }

scenarios.description: An absent selector over a document holding several operation definitions reaches no addressable target: the invocation refuses at resolution.
A selector naming no operation definition does not resolve: the invocation refuses at resolution.
Names compare by exact code points: a selector differing only in case names no operation definition.
An unused fragment fails §5.5.1.4 and invalidates the whole inventory: a sibling operation resolves and refuses before dispatch.
A directive the interpreted schema does not define fails §5.7.1; the document is sent as carried or not at all, so every operation refuses before dispatch.

content.document:
query Status { status @connection(key: "s") }
query Viewer($id: ID!) { viewer(id: $id) { id } }

scenarios.description: A directive the interpreted schema defines validates, and the document dispatches with the directive carried as written.

content.document: query Status { status @cache(ttl: 5) }

scenarios.description: A mutation operation against a schema with no mutation root fails §5.2.1.1, which is inventory-wide like every §5 rule: the query sibling refuses before dispatch.

content.document:
query Status { status }
mutation Rename($id: ID!, $name: String!) { rename(id: $id, name: $name) { id } }
content.schema:
type Query { status: String }
type User { id: ID! }

scenarios.description: A September 2025 tightening applies to every service: @skip on a subscription's root selection set (§5.2.4.1) invalidates the inventory, so the query sibling refuses before dispatch.

content.document:
query Status { status }
subscription Ticks { ticks @skip(if: false) }
content.schema:
type Query { status: String }
type Subscription { ticks: Int }

scenarios.description: A meta-field selection validates against §4.2's introspection types, not the carried type set: it dispatches against a schema whose types omit them.

content.document: query M { __schema { queryType { name } } }

scenarios.description: A service-added validation rule rejects a document this specification accepted: the service's request error is an unsuccessful completion with no output, not a defect.
